core.title: Declare a deterministic route resolution strategy for every flow router
core.given: A user/system flow plan contains a flow router, whether newly authored, edited, or unchanged by the current task.
core.when: The planner authors or changes that flow router, or the plan is validated at the confirmation phase (CONFIRM).
core.then: The flow router must explicitly declare a deterministic route resolution strategy—fail_on_multiple_match, or first_priority with unique integer priorities on its routes—so that ambiguous matching routes fail closed unless resolved by those declared unique priorities.
prefer: Write the strategy name explicitly on the flow router, using exactly one of the two allowed strategies.
When choosing first_priority, give every route a unique integer priority.
avoid: Leaving the strategy implicit, or relying on declaration order or any other undeclared tie-break to pick a route.
Declaring first_priority with duplicate, missing, or non-integer route priorities.
Using strategy names other than fail_on_multiple_match and first_priority.
core.why: Route resolution must be explicit and deterministic: when several routes match, the flow router must fail closed unless a declared unique priority resolves the ambiguity, rather than picking a route arbitrarily.
evidence: The plan-coherence check for this rule passes at the confirmation phase for every flow router in the plan, changed or not.
On failure, the finding reports the flow router id, the declared strategy (or its absence), the route ids with their priorities, and the reason.
verification: Enforced by a plan-coherence validation whose subject is the flow router: every flow router in the plan is evaluated, and only non-compliant ones produce a finding (a finding means non-compliance, not mere applicability).
Checked at the confirmation phase (CONFIRM); enforcement is confirm-blocking, so a finding blocks plan confirmation.
Severity 4; disposition strict: no baseline or advisory reading, and the 'unless resolved by declared unique priorities' clause in the obligation is a resolution mode of first_priority, not a waiver.
Out of scope: plans that contain no flow router at all, and edits that touch only artifacts that are not flow routers before confirmation-phase validation.

values: flow router route resolution strategy undeclared or non-compliant

fires: A plan reaches the confirmation phase and contains any flow router, including flow routers unchanged by the current task; each is evaluated (applicability), and only non-compliant ones produce a finding.
A planner authors or edits a flow router or its routes.
A flow router has no declared route resolution strategy (non-compliant).
A flow router declares first_priority but its routes' priorities are duplicated, missing, or non-integer (non-compliant).
A flow router declares fail_on_multiple_match, or first_priority with unique integer priorities: the rule still applies and the flow router is evaluated, and it passes.
doesNotFire: A plan that contains no flow router subject at all.
Plan edits touching only artifacts that are not flow routers, before confirmation-phase validation (e.g. product capability or acceptance wording that does not define a flow router).
Broad 'user/system flow' or 'route' task terms alone, without a flow router as the subject, do not identify the scope.

bunOnly.text: Validator test_sequence_diagram_sanity::test_flow_router_route_resolution_strategy_declared passes at CONFIRM for every flow router in the plan.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention lives in the plan language (user/system flow plans, flow routers, routes, priority strategies, the CONFIRM phase), which is shared across stacks rather than being code-stack machinery, so the core keeps those domain terms verbatim — including the strategy names fail_on_multiple_match and first_priority, which carry the exact obligation — and Bun contributes only the realization ids (validator test, validation family/template/variant, finding id) via bunOnly. No structure-profile data (paths, suffixes, roots, idioms, tooling) is needed, so profileRequirements is empty and no keys are proposed. The activation facts' 'note' fields have no place in the neutral fact shape; their nuances (hint-only task terms, confirm-blocking evaluation of every flow router, finding-means-non-compliance) are preserved in activation.fires/doesNotFire and verification.
